title: Inquisitor
author: Ian Watson (I don’t understand how Steven Spielberg could have looked at this sewer goblin’s prior work and thought “hey, I’ll get this guy to write a screenplay for my next movie”. I am unfortunately not joking about that in the slightest. This weirdo actually wrote the screen story for Steven Spielberg’s “A.I.”. After “Inquisitor”, I suspect Ian Watson was a big reason why “A.I.” became such a waste of otherwise great potential.)

title: Armada
author: Ernest Cline (“Ready Player One” wasn’t perfect, but this took all the worst aspects of that book (and JUST the worst aspects), and turned them into some kind of Frankenstein’s monster of a novel.)

title: Fifty Shades of Grey
author: E. L. James (I don’t think the Glibert Gottfried reading takes away from the tone at all. This is some “Inquisitor”-level (see #3) ANTI-aphrodisiac here)

author: L Ron Hubbard (Well, at least reading this removed any motivation to have anything to do with the Scientiology cult. That’s at least one bullet dodged.)

author: L Ron Hubbard (I don’t know why I thought the book was going to be better than the movie)

title: Rama II
author: Gentry Lee & Arthur C. Clarke (There was such a dramatic drop in quality between the 1st and 2nd books that I was worried)

title: The Garden of Rama
author: Gentry Lee & Arthur C. Clarke (God…dammit…God fucking dammit, Arthur.)

title: The Number of the Beast
author: Robert Heinlein (I powered through this book hoping that there was going to be some kind of worthwhile ending. There are so many ways my limited time in this life could have been better spent.)

title: Fire with Fire
author: Charles Gannon (Were the 2014 Nebula Awards judges bribed?)

title: Left Behind: A Novel of the Earth’s Last Days
author: Tim LaHaye and Jerry B. Jenkins (I tried to be open-minded and look at some “christian” fiction. It turns out this was one of the worst possibe starting points. This is the kind of Kirk-Cameron-death-to-all-not-part-of-my-subdenomination christianity that turns people into atheists.)

title: Timeline
author: Michael Chrichton (I used to think Deepak Chopra was bad with the whole “Quantum = Magic” schtick. It turns out he could have done so much worse.)

title: Forever Free
author: Joe Haldeman (Why do such amazing science fiction books keep getting such aggressively horrible sequels?)

title: The Lair of the White Worm
author: Bram Stoker (What the hell happened to Bran Stoker between this and “Dracula”?)

title: The Eye of Argon
author: Jim Theis (Actually read this at a party (one where a LOT of alcohol was involved). This “The Room” of books. Even H.P. Lovecraft would look at this book and say “This author’s just going too overboard with the flowery descriptions”)
